name: Provincial Nominee Program (PNP)

selection_odds.basis: 2026 PNP-specific CRS cutoffs run 708-768 (high because a provincial nomination adds a flat +600 CRS points). National PNP allocation for 2026 is 91,500, up from 55,000 in 2025.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires nomination by a specific province or territory through that jurisdiction's own PNP stream, each of which runs its own occupation priorities and sometimes its own points thresholds.
requirements.fix_path: Apply through the relevant province/territory's own PNP stream.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires meeting the base Express Entry eligibility criteria of one of FSWP, CEC, or FSTP, in addition to the provincial nomination itself.

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL DIVERGENCE confirmed mid-2026: Ontario (OINP) REVOKED all nine legacy streams on 30 May 2026 (O. Reg. 47/26), rebuilding around targeted draws plus mandatory employer registration, with a new Ontario Workforce Priority stream launched 26 June 2026; master's/PhD graduate streams were eliminated entirely. British Columbia's allocation was cut to 5,254 for 2026, far below the ~9,000 the province had requested. National allocation raised to 91,500 for 2026 (up from 55,000 in 2025) — a genuinely large year-over-year increase running counter to Canada's broader 2026-2028 immigration-reduction trend, worth flagging as a real internal inconsistency: overall PR targets are frozen/reduced while PNP specifically expanded. The +600 CRS bonus from nomination functions as a near-guarantee of an ITA at the next relevant draw — the most reliable single lever in Canada's points system for anyone who can secure a nomination.
